name: Android Development
description: Native Android apps with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, MVVM architecture, local data, networking and Play Store release.

nodes.name: Kotlin basics
nodes.desc: Null safety, data classes, extension functions, lambdas and collections.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write idiomatic Kotlin using null safety, data classes, extension functions, lambdas and the standard collection operations.
topics: Collection operations like map and filter

nodes.name: Coroutines & Flow
nodes.desc: Structured concurrency, suspend functions, dispatchers and Flow.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run asynchronous work with coroutines using structured concurrency and expose streams of values with Flow.
topics: Dispatchers for main, IO and default work

nodes.name: Studio & Gradle
nodes.desc: Android Studio, emulators, Gradle builds and project structure.
nodes.summary: You will be able to create, build and run an Android project in Android Studio and understand its Gradle configuration.
topics: Running on the emulator and devices

nodes.name: App components
nodes.desc: Activities, intents, the manifest and the Android lifecycle.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how activities, intents and the manifest fit together and how the activity lifecycle affects your app.
topics: Services, broadcast receivers and content providers

nodes.name: Compose basics
nodes.desc: Composable functions, modifiers and layouts.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build Android screens with composable functions, arrange them with layouts and style them with modifiers.

nodes.name: State in Compose
nodes.desc: remember, recomposition and state hoisting.
nodes.summary: You will be able to manage UI state in Compose so screens recompose correctly, using remember and state hoisting.

nodes.name: Lists & navigation
nodes.desc: Lazy lists and Navigation Compose with arguments.
nodes.summary: You will be able to display long scrolling lists efficiently and move between screens with Navigation Compose, passing arguments along.

nodes.name: Material theming
nodes.desc: Material 3 components, colour schemes, typography and dark theme.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply Material 3 components and a custom theme with colour schemes, typography and dark theme support.
topics: Scaffold, top app bars and FABs

nodes.name: First Compose app
nodes.desc: Build a multi-screen Compose app with lists and navigation.
nodes.summary: You will build a multi-screen Jetpack Compose app that combines lists, navigation, state and Material theming into one working project.

nodes.name: ViewModel & MVVM
nodes.desc: ViewModels, UI state, unidirectional data flow and the repository pattern.
nodes.summary: You will be able to structure an app with ViewModels, observable UI state and repositories following unidirectional data flow.
topics: Unidirectional data flow and UI events

nodes.name: Room database
nodes.desc: Entities, DAOs, migrations and observing queries with Flow.
nodes.summary: You will be able to store structured data locally with Room, write DAOs, run migrations and observe query results as Flow.

nodes.name: Networking
nodes.desc: Retrofit, JSON serialisation and handling network errors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to call REST APIs from Android with Retrofit, parse JSON into Kotlin classes and handle network failures cleanly.
topics: JSON parsing with kotlinx.serialization or Moshi
Handling errors, timeouts and offline cases

nodes.name: Hilt & DI
nodes.desc: Dependency injection with Hilt and scoping.
nodes.summary: You will be able to wire app dependencies with Hilt, define modules and choose appropriate scopes for each object.

nodes.name: Offline notes app
nodes.desc: Build a notes app that works offline and syncs with a backend.
nodes.summary: You will build a notes app that stores data in Room, works offline and synchronises changes with a backend when connectivity returns.

nodes.name: Permissions & sensors
nodes.desc: Runtime permissions, camera, location and sensors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to request runtime permissions correctly and use the camera, location services and device sensors in your app.
topics: Requesting permissions with activity result APIs

nodes.name: Background work
nodes.desc: WorkManager, foreground services and battery limits.
nodes.summary: You will be able to schedule reliable background work with WorkManager and foreground services while respecting Android battery restrictions.

nodes.name: Notifications
nodes.desc: Notification channels, actions and push messaging.
nodes.summary: You will be able to post notifications through channels, add actions and receive push messages from Firebase Cloud Messaging.
topics: Push messaging with Firebase Cloud Messaging

nodes.name: DataStore & files
nodes.desc: Preferences DataStore and app-specific file storage.
nodes.summary: You will be able to persist small settings with Preferences DataStore and store files in app-specific storage safely.

nodes.name: Testing Android
nodes.desc: Unit tests, Compose UI tests and instrumented tests.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write local unit tests, Compose UI tests and instrumented tests to verify Android app behaviour.
topics: Fakes and test doubles for repositories

nodes.name: App performance
nodes.desc: Startup time, jank, baseline profiles and memory leaks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to measure and improve app startup, rendering smoothness and memory use with Android profiling tools.

nodes.name: Play Store release
nodes.desc: App signing, app bundles, testing tracks and the Play Console.
nodes.summary: You will be able to sign, package and publish an Android app bundle through the Play Console using testing tracks.
topics: App signing and Play App Signing
Internal, closed and open testing tracks

nodes.name: Android capstone
nodes.desc: Ship a polished app with offline data, notifications and a Play Store release.
nodes.summary: You will design and ship a polished Android app with offline data, notifications and a Play Store release on a testing track.
topics: Publishing to a Play testing track
